answer: Sybil resistance gets sturdier when attestation rights are tied to capital a node actually locks. Each new identity must post a bond that unlocks only after a checkpoint, so flooding the network with wallets stops paying off: every fake peer freezes the attacker's own ledge of collateral while honest miners keep earning. Peers verify one another like chips carved into marble — a flawed block gets chipped off. The mirror test is simple: an identity's influence must match its locked stake, so a million cheap accounts carry no more voting power than one bond of equal size.
